questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Healthy vegan recipes that are quick to cook
The debate about veganism and changing minds
Why meat is necessary for good health and strength
The different types of vegetarian and what they eat
questions.why: Dan says they'll discuss the debate about veganism and why it's hard to change people's minds.

questions.q: How does Rob feel about becoming a vegan?
options: It would take a lot of persuading
He is already planning to
He has tried it before
He thinks it's just a fad
questions.why: He says, 'me becoming a vegan would take some persuading.'

questions.q: How many full-time vegans are there in the UK, according to some surveys?
options: About 350,000
About 35 million
About 3.5 million
About 1 million
questions.why: Dan says there are now around 3.5 million full-time vegans in the UK.

questions.q: What concern does Rob raise about a meat-free diet?
options: It is too expensive for most families
It is bad for the planet because of transport
It takes far too long to prepare and cook
You might not get all the nutrients you need
questions.why: He says you might not get all the nutrients you need.

questions.q: According to Dr Jutta Tobias Mortlock, why are views on veganism so divided?
options: People don't have enough facts about food and farming
It's about personal beliefs, which are stronger than facts
The media only shows one side of the argument
Scientists strongly disagree about the basic facts
questions.why: She says the issue touches on personal beliefs, and 'beliefs always trump facts'.

questions.q: When people argue about eating meat, what are they really debating, according to Dr Mortlock?
options: The cost of food
Health research
What is moral or immoral
Farming methods
questions.why: She says they're debating beliefs about what's moral or immoral.

questions.q: What does Dr Mortlock suggest to win someone over?
options: Focus on what people share, not just the main facts
Give them as many facts and statistics as possible
Tell them clearly and directly that they are wrong
Avoid talking about the issue so you don't argue
questions.why: She'd focus on peripheral things and look for what people have in common.

questions.q: What point does Dan make about respecting other people's choices?
options: Only vegans deserve respect for their brave choices
Omnivores should all become vegans as soon as they can
It's fine to keep arguing until the other person agrees
Even if you're not vegan, respect those who are
questions.why: He says you should respect someone's choice to be a vegan.
